paper_metadata.title: Synergistic effects of Hf and Ta on strength-ductility in refractory high-entropy alloys: Kink band formation and dislocation evolution

evidence.quote: a Ti35Zr35Nb10Hf10Ta10 RHEA was designed through tailored microstructural and dislocation behavior control.
Similar phenomena are observed in other RHEAs and the TZN alloy (Figs. S4-S8), where the size and morphology of kink bands vary in response to grain refinement.

In summary, the plastic deformation mechanisms of as-cast Ti-Zr-Nb-Hf-Ta RHEAs were systematically analyzed, with a focus on the microstructure evolution of the Ti35Zr35Nb10Hf10Ta10 RHEA (YS:~1 GPa, El:25.6 %, UTS:16.5 %, E:54.6 GPa) at different deformation stages.

The button-shaped ingots were then remelted and cast by gravity into a water-cooled copper mold to form rectangular ingots of 10 × 10 × 60 mm3.

evidence.section: 3.3. Microstructure of Hf10Ta10 at different deformation stages
evidence.quote: The as-cast Hf10Ta10 exhibits an equiaxed dendritic microstructures with slight compositional segregation (Figs. 3a and S2).
Their combined effect induces pronounced local chemical fluctuations, which promote dislocation pinning, stable strain hardening, and cross-slip activity.

Further TEM observations of the submicron-scale deformation microstructure during the necking stage confirm that the alloy retains its β-BCC single-phase structure without any phase transformation (inset in Fig. 6a).
Additionally, wide and straight dislocation channels along the (1–11) plane are observed, containing extensive dislocation entanglement and interactions.
Furthermore, a substantial number of dislocation loops are observed.

attributes.location: within grains, some cross grain boundaries

evidence.section: 3.4. Details of kink bands in deformed Hf10Ta10
evidence.quote: The distribution and morphology of deformation bands after tensile fracture (Fig. 8a) indicate that these bands are elongated and vary in number across different grains. While most deformation bands are confined within individual grains, some extend across grain boundaries, connecting adjacent grains.

This activation corresponds to the formation of kink bands, which play a crucial role in redistributing internal stress concentrations within the grains.
As illustrated in Fig. 12 e and f, dislocation slip traces (110) terminate at kink band boundaries, indicating that kink bands act as barriers to dislocation motion, thereby restricting local slip.
the activation of the {110} slip system leads to the accumulation of a/2 < 111 > {110} edge dislocations at the kink band boundaries.

evidence.section: 4.1. Effect of Hf and Ta on mechanical properties of RHEAs
evidence.quote: This observation explains the presence of dislocation loops during both the yielding and necking stages of Hf10Ta10, which are attributed primarily to the pinning effect of LCFs.
Initially, planar slip dominates, however, as the tensile process progresses, slip resistance increases, leading to a gradual transition to cross-slip and multisystem slip as the primary mechanism.
